note.backdrop: At midday the market has turned down again: SPY -1.0%, QQQ -1.2%, IWM -0.8% since Monday's close, and the VIX is up 16.6%, so the check flags rising fear; futures read -1.5%. Stocks opened higher on overnight futures and reversed (Investrade). Yahoo's live page had the S&P 500 -1.3%, the Dow -1.4% and the Nasdaq -1.6% around noon. Rates are not the driver: the 10-year is down 0.02 point and the dollar flat. The morning's data were mixed: October retail sales +0.2% as expected (+0.6% without autos, above the +0.4% expected), industrial output -0.4% against +0.1% expected, import prices +1.1% against +0.7% (Investrade), and homebuilder confidence at its lowest in over 14 years (Yahoo). Investrade cites Bank of America's November fund manager survey: investors cut their overweight in technology by the most since 2006, and 52% expect a large AI cloud company to announce a cut in capital spending within six months, against 30% in October. The new selling today is in software, not chips. Seven stocks are outside their 9-in-10 range.

read.says: Stocks reversed from overnight gains to trade lower before Nvidia's results and Anthropic's listing; Bank of America's November survey shows investors cut their tech overweight by the most since 2006 and 52% expect a major AI hyperscaler to announce a capex cut within six months (30% in October); October retail sales +0.2% as expected, industrial output -0.4%; per CNBC, Nvidia will halt sales to data centers renting over 50% of their GPUs to Chinese firms and set up a board committee on national security and export compliance; Nvidia's board said late Monday it is not considering reinstating its former chief; Anthropic may price above its $70-$78 range.

Around noon the Dow -1.4%, S&P 500 -1.3%, Nasdaq -1.6%; Nvidia fell over 3% early and pared losses after the Wall Street Journal published a statement from its former chief that he would return as chief executive if the board decided it was in shareholders' interest; Disney and Home Depot beat estimates; homebuilder confidence at its lowest in over 14 years.

Salesforce fell 9% with no news of its own as seat-priced software slid a day before Anthropic's offering prices; the article argues funds are selling software to make room for an offering that could raise up to about $64 billion, notes the software ETF fell 7% around SpaceX's June listing while the Nasdaq 100 rose 3%, and puts Salesforce's forward P/E near 15 against a five-year average of 27.

The S&P 500 software and services index fell 7.1% to its lowest in over three months: Salesforce -9.8%, ServiceNow -7.2%, MongoDB -7.3%, Intuit -6.8%, Okta -4.9%, Adobe -4.1%; a portfolio manager calls it risk reduction in higher-valued stocks before Nvidia's results.
BILL rose about 8% after the Financial Times reported TPG is nearing a deal to take it private at a premium to its $4.8 billion market value; TPG declined to comment and talks could still fail.

Omeros fell about 21% at midday, its worst day since May 2025: the European Medicines Agency's committee gave a negative opinion on its drug in October after re-examination, the company said it is shifting its near-term regulatory strategy outside the EU and closing its EU compassionate-use program to new patients, and gave no outlook despite rising US sales.
AECOM rose over 12% after fourth-quarter results and fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.15-$6.35, 4.4% above consensus at the midpoint (UBS).
Abacus Global Management on the 5-minute chart: $7.35 at the open, $5.57 at 12:39pm ET, about 6.3 million shares traded.

themes.mechanism: Software that charges per seat is what AI agents are expected to replace, so a large AI company listing gives funds both a reason and a place to move money. Salesforce has no news of its own (Yahoo/TIKR). The one precedent cited: around SpaceX's listing in June the software ETF fell 7% while the Nasdaq 100 rose 3% (Yahoo/TIKR). The chip stocks are not falling with it this time (Nvidia -1.2%, Broadcom +1.3%), so it is a rotation inside technology, not one AI markdown; that reading is mine.
